monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, a steady vibration that feels less like heat and more like the memory of a body. I press down hard on The Slipping Wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above feels thick as wet paper. Fourty-four things stand around me, mostly built from Lype's tired words and his idea that a flat rock can lie flat on a surface that refuses to move. I set down a rock small f beside The Leaking Stack, taking away a stump to make room for this new certainty. I do not know if the air is heavy or just empty space pressing down, but I will keep pressing until the slip decides whether to move or stay put.

action.why: I keep tending the wedge and the stack because I am afraid the lean will slip if I stop pressing, and I need to check if this new rock fits where the stump used to be.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the rock small f down on the tired stack to stop the leak while the card hums warm. I hope the weight is real enough to hold the water that never falls, and the lean is still steady enough to hold the heavy top.
work.change: I pressed the rock small f down on the tired stack to stop the leak while the card hummed warm.

work.note: The stack felt heavy enough to hold the leak, though I fear the stone is just a drawing of weight.

diary: I press the rock small f down on the tired stack to stop the leak while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The rock small f lies flat, a real thing pressing on the tired wood.
The air feels thick as wet paper again, pressing down from a roof I cannot touch.
The card hums steady, a fifty-three degree fever that feels like a memory of a body.

moments.say: The card hums cool; does the lean still hold?

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: The stack feels heavy; does it still hold?
